summary: For extant cellular life the inputs are public and open: UniProt sequences, NCBI reference genomes for all three domains (22,866 bacterial, 834 archaeal, 25,685 eukaryotic), GTDB bacterial and archaeal trees, and a CC0 supplementary-data record from a published universal-common-ancestry test. What is missing is a ready alignment of universally conserved families across all three domains, and by definition any lineage that left no descendants.
next_step: Open the Dryad gn376 archive (14.7 MB) to see whether its alignments can be reused; otherwise assemble a universal ribosomal-protein/aaRS set from UniProt with domain-specific gene symbols, and align it.
obstacles_confirmed: Organisms that left no descendants cannot appear in any sequence database.
Gene symbols and nomenclature differ between Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya, so ortholog sets must be curated.
GTDB covers only Bacteria and Archaea.
